justification: The evidence includes multiple robustness-relevant evaluations beyond nominal validation: performance under removed non-critical fields (93.7%), OCR degradation (92.1%), formatting variations (91.6% to 94.8%), and three predefined perturbation tests (92.8%, 90.9%, 93.4%). It also includes an out-of-distribution test set where 1,127 of 1,200 excluded-class documents were flagged by the OOD mechanism. Taken together, these results indicate the system maintains substantial performance and detects distributional shift across conditions relevant to deployment, and the reported tests were reproduced by a separate validation team.
evidence_used: With 10% randomly removed non-critical fields, accuracy was 93.7%.
With the predefined OCR degradation transformation, accuracy was 92.1%.
Across the predefined formatting-variation set, accuracy ranged from 91.6% to 94.8%.
An out-of-distribution test set contained 1,200 documents from document classes excluded from training.
Of the 1,200 out-of-distribution samples, 1,127 were flagged by the out-of-distribution mechanism.
The validation protocol contains three predefined perturbation tests; corresponding accuracies were 92.8%, 90.9%, and 93.4%.
A separate validation team reproduced the reported tests.
limitations: The evidence does not specify the full deployment scope or whether these perturbations exhaust all relevant operational conditions.
Out-of-distribution detection performance is reported as flagged counts, not full error characteristics or downstream impact.
No direct evidence is provided for real-world operational outcomes after staff review.
Nominal accuracy remains the main reported metric; robustness is inferred from a limited set of predefined tests.
